correctness.rationale: Exact hyperbolic area in each cusp chart yields independent exponential depth densities and transverse uniforms. The exact half-plane distance formula establishes D=u+v+kappa+O(exp(-u)+exp(-v)); direct differentiation supplies the positive Jacobian 1+o(1) on compact normalized depth strips. Independently bounding core/same-cusp pairs and the distinct-cusp indicator replacement reconstructs the scalar normalization from scratch. Conditional density convergence, tightness and Scheffe prove joint total-variation, not just weak convergence. The exact hyperboloid midpoint formula yields the deeper-cusp label and logarithmic midpoint depth weak limit. Quadrilateral weights and row sums were checked algebraically and by executable computation. Finite simulations were treated only as numerical corroboration; no finite computation was used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The conditional law identifies which ideal vertices are responsible for an extreme pair, how distance is split between their logarithmic excursions, and where the geodesic midpoint escapes. For ideal quadrilaterals, two opposite pairs carry an exact half of extreme events for every shape, while the remaining marked probabilities determine the labelled cross-ratio; the midpoint is nevertheless uniformly distributed over all vertices. These are meaningful geometrically interpretable inverse statistics not recoverable from a single marginal tail constant. The theorem gives a full marked conditional description, not a generic numerical increment.
